comparison: Perfect alignment on device design claims (C9-C15, C49-C52). Both evaluations find the device mechanism, toroidal geometry, volume measurements, and droplet retention features well-supported. OpenEval cites Figure 1 and supplements; peer reviewers explicitly praise the 'engineered device' and 'technical innovations in liquid handling.'

Perfect alignment on photoinitiation superiority (C16-C17, C24). Both evaluations accept the comparative data showing APS/TEMED inconsistency and Irgacure 2959 superiority. OpenEval references Figure 2 supplement 3; peer reviewers acknowledge 'modifications to how the expandable hydrogels are polymerized' without challenge.

Perfect alignment on fluorophore photobleaching (C18, C42). Both evaluations support the differential effects on fluorophores and CF dye recommendation. OpenEval cites Figure 1 supplement 4 with quantitative data; peer reviewers implicitly accept by not raising concerns.

Perfect alignment on Irgacure concentration optimization (C19, C59). Both evaluations accept the titration data and optimal concentration findings. OpenEval references Figure 1 supplement 5; peer reviewers treat as accepted methodological details.

Partial overlap on expansion characterization. OpenEval R5 addresses expansion factor and uniformity (C3, C26-C29) with statistical support from Figure 2g-h. Peer R6 addresses overlapping claims (C3, C20, C26-C27, C45) including resolution improvement. Both find evidence sufficient, though OpenEval notes the variability mechanism (C29) is speculative.

Focused agreement on between-plate variability (C28-C29). Both evaluations acknowledge the variability and accept the evaporation-based explanation. OpenEval provides statistical details (ANOVA); peer reviewers note this doesn't undermine the method's utility.

Perfect alignment on expansion isotropy and distortion analysis (C22-C23, C25, C47, C67-C70). Both evaluations strongly support the non-rigid registration findings. OpenEval cites Figure 2d-f with quantitative metrics; peer reviewers praise the 'thorough characterization of impressive expansion isotropy.'

Partial overlap on resolution improvement (C20-C21, C45). OpenEval R7 focuses on decorrelation analysis showing ~4-fold improvement. Peer R6 includes these claims alongside expansion factor validation, explicitly affirming 'robust ~4-fold expansion' without challenge.

Strong alignment on high-throughput automation (C4, C44, C62-C65, C81). Both evaluations support the automated workflow and compatibility with commercial systems. OpenEval notes 3-64 hr time range variability; peer reviewers strongly affirm 'clear path towards high throughput exM' and note timing information was added per reviewer request.

Perfect alignment on doxorubicin application (C5, C32-C35, C74-C76). Both evaluations support the dose-dependent chromatin changes and improved sensitivity post-expansion. OpenEval notes mechanistic interpretation relies on literature inference; peer reviewers describe this as 'solid proof-of-concept' with effects 'only detectable by ExM.'

Perfect alignment on H2O2 control experiment (C36). Both evaluations view this negative control as strengthening the doxorubicin findings. OpenEval notes different stressor limits direct comparability; peer reviewers specifically praise this comparison as significantly strengthening conclusions.

Perfect alignment on doxorubicin literature context (C30-C31). Both evaluations accept these background claims about doxorubicin effects without challenge. OpenEval cites multiple references; peer reviewers treat as established background motivating experimental design.

Perfect alignment on alternative chemistry compatibility (C43, C55-C56). Both evaluations support the platform's flexibility for different expansion chemistries. OpenEval references Figure 3 supplement 6 and citations; peer reviewers accept this as methodological advantage extending utility.

Strong alignment on accessibility and versatility (C37, C39-C41, C77, C80). Both evaluations support claims about fabrication methods and adaptability. OpenEval notes simplicity/cost claims are subjective; peer reviewers emphasize broad applicability and describe technology as 'extremely useful.'

Divergent evaluations on theoretical resolution prediction (C46). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting lack of experimental validation despite theoretical soundness. Peer R17 groups this with other methodological details and accepts without question, treating as standard technical information.

Contrasting evaluations on gel detachment artifact (C57-C58). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, accepting that infrequent occurrence doesn't impact interpretation. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, with one reviewer expressing persistent concern about whether unexpanded cells remain in wells, noting this 'is still a concern that potential users should be aware of.'

Alignment on manual curation limitation (C66). OpenEval explicitly identifies this as a practical limitation affecting throughput. Peer R17 groups this with other methodological details and accepts without specific critique, treating as standard technical information.

Strong alignment on computational methods (C82-C88). Both evaluations accept the analytical approaches with appropriate citations. OpenEval notes manual curation introduces potential bias and limits scalability; peer reviewers treat these as standard methods not requiring additional validation.

Strong alignment on foundational background (C1, C6-C8, C71-C72). Both evaluations support these contextual claims about super-resolution microscopy and expansion microscopy principles. OpenEval cites foundational papers; peer reviewers accept without question, with editor affirming the study 'develops a high throughput version of expansion microscopy.'

Strong alignment on comparison to related work (C38, C78-C79). Both evaluations support the characterization of HiExM advantages over alternatives. OpenEval notes C79 is speculation about future applications; peer reviewers explicitly affirm advantages over Reference 8 regarding standard plate compatibility.

Partial overlap on practical imaging considerations (C54, C60-C61). OpenEval R20 addresses gel coverage and 3D imaging implications. Peer R9 focuses on high-throughput capability but includes overlapping claims about imaging workflow. Both accept these as practical aspects of the method.

Minimal overlap on gel coverage measurement (C48). OpenEval R20 groups this with imaging implications. Peer R18 treats gel coverage as accepted factual technical detail alongside basic ExM principles (C71). Both accept without challenge.

Minimal overlap on photoinitiator compatibility (C53). OpenEval R2 includes this in photoinitiation superiority evaluation. Peer R13 groups with alternative chemistry compatibility. Both accept as supporting platform flexibility.
